text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- Japan's Isuzu diesel engine firm, controlled by General Motors, plans to invest up to 500 million marks in the Katowice special economic zone in southern Poland.
- The National Bank of Poland (NBP), the central bank, has provisonally allowed German Berliner Bank to start operations in Poland.
If accepted by the Finance Ministry, the bank will soon receive an operating licence issued by the NBP president.
- Poland's largest insurance firm PZU will be privatised in 1997's first quarter, finance ministry representatives said.
- The Gdynia shipyard will hand over two container ships to German contractors KG Projex and Alpha Ship GmbH.
In 1996 the shipyard will construct nine ships worth $300 million.
- Lengthy legal procedures for marking out future motorway routes may lead to delays in Polnd's motorway programme, Transport Minister Boguslaw Liberadzki said.
- Potato prices declined in September while all other agricultural prices rose, the Central Statistics Office (GUS) said.
- Nissan Almera passenger cars made in Britain will be available to Polish buyers within the 1997 duty-free import quotas, a Polish Nissan dealer said.
- The listed TC Debica tyre maker has recently opened a branch office in Budapest as part of its international development strategy, the plant's marketing director Andrzej Stelmach said. NOWA EUROPA
- In June Poland's unemployment was greatest in the regions of Katowice (6.1 percent), Kielce (3.8 percent), Bydgoszcz (3.6 percent) and Lodz (3.5 percent), GUS said.
- Over 40 bicycle and cycling equipment makers from Poland and abroad will exhibit their products at the Poznan-based International Bicycle Fair, Bicykl '96, to start on October 19.
- The right-wing Movement for the Reconstruction of Poland (ROP) proposed to set up retirement funds based on shares in the largest state-owned firms.
ROP called the plan to fund old-age pensions from the privatisation of the KGHM Polska Miedz Copper conglomerate a "penny-worth meat slice" pitifully thrown to the retired.
- Many unresolved commercial issues between the EU and Poland stand in the way of Poland's quick entry to the European Union, EU economic experts say.
- Preliminary financial data for Poland's insurance sector for the third quarter show that the sector's crisis is over, participants of the Third Insurance Congress in Warsaw said. GAZETA WYBORCZA
- Poland's milk production has declined in October, the agricultural products processing and acqusition agency said.

High quality milk prices ranged from 0.48 zloty a litre in Zielona Gora province to 0.78 zloty in Lomza province, while the price of quality butter was 0.17 zloty per kilogramme higher in the first week of October than in the week before.
- Poland's Supreme Administrative Court has awarded to the Maczki Bor sand mine property rights for the site of the Polish-Russian Topgas liquid fuel reloading station.
The station's construction cost Topgas $10 million and was the biggest Russian capital investment in central Europe, Topgas representatives said.
ZYCIE WARSZAWY
- The left-wing Union of Labour's (UP) party congress re-elected Ryszard Bugaj as chairman.
The congress decided that the party will not participate in any coalition before the next parliamentary elections.

- Environmental activists from Krakow, Poznan and Lodz protested against the government motorway construction programme in Warsaw yesterday. The environmentalists want railway transport investments to replace the motorway scheme.
